A1.justification: Both complete 27-page PDFs describe RAVEN and AVS-QA. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAVEN benchmark results, ablations, corruption experiments, and a human evaluation of 300 AVS-QA examples in Appendix B.3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a frame-selection experiment in Appendix G, Table 12.

M1.justification: The RAVEN/QuART architecture, relevance scoring, losses, three-stage training, and dataset-curation pipeline remain unchanged. Alternative frame-selection strategies appear as evaluation ablations; uniform sampling remains the default.

E1.justification: Training sources, the seven external QA benchmarks, AVS-QA evaluation, and modality-corruption coverage are retained. The new sampling experiment uses six existing benchmarks and changes preprocessing within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated baseline sets remain unchanged. The ImageBind, MBT, and AVFIC comparison in v1 Table 12 is preserved as v3 Table 13; the new sampling rows are within-RAVEN ablation variants.

E3.justification: v3 adds an evaluation protocol comparing random, fixed-stride, uniform, and oracle frame selection across six benchmarks. Existing splits, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a focused sensitivity study testing how frame selection affects QA performance. Earlier training-stage, encoder, LoRA-rank, relevance-projection and fusion studies, corruption tests, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: The new experiment reports point scores without adding seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its statement about increased variability under random sampling supplies no statistical estimate or procedure.

E6.justification: v3 Table 12 adds random, fixed-stride, and oracle sampling scores: for example, MSVD-QA scores are 50.7, 72.9, and 73.4, respectively. The uniform score remains 73.3; existing benchmark results and qualitative examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The dataset mapping, attention and relevance equations, training objective in Equation 1, and mismatch-generation formalization are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: query-guided multimodal fusion, three-stage training, AVS-QA, and improved QA robustness. Their headline performance and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets the sampling results as showing resilience to frame selection, with random sampling problematic and oracle selection offering limited benefits. Section 8's existing limitation concerning missed visual cues in long videos remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The added discussion states that oracle selection uses salient-frame annotations and metadata from EPIC-Kitchens-100 and Ego4D. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds EgoAdapt (Chowdhury et al., 2025) to the introduction and citations to Mohapatra et al. (2024) and Biswas et al. (2023) under 'Missingness resilient' in Appendix A. These are limited additions without broader repositioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds an equal-contribution footnote, acknowledgments, and a short frame-selection discussion, and updates several bibliography author lists. The overall section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds a full-width sampling table and relocates the existing fusion comparison as Table 13. Local reflow changes figure/text placement, including Appendix I, while existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: v1 identified uniform sampling as a possible limitation but provided no sampling ablation. v3 Table 12 adds useful evidence that fixed-stride and uniform sampling perform similarly while random sampling performs substantially worse. The gain is limited: the oracle description does not explain how Ego4D/EPIC-Kitchens metadata supports the listed benchmarks, small oracle gains lack uncertainty estimates, and the long-video limitation remains unresolved.
